[conversational] This boring contact form tool makes $44K every single month.

[serious] These numbers are verified on TrustMRR: $44K MRR, $45K in the last 30 days, 3,204 active subscriptions, and about 412,000 users. Bootstrapped, started December 2020.

But it wasn't fast. In February 2021, revenue was $101.60, with 11 paid users.

So what can you steal? One: build the tool you can't find. Two: a free plan, 250 submissions a month, as your funnel.

[whispers] He put effort into SEO from the early days, writing content for related searches, and today he says Google is his number 1 channel.

The honest catch? It's a crowded market, and growth is about 1% a month now.

[curious] Would you build this, or buy it? Send this to the friend who keeps saying every good idea is already taken. Hack saved?

topic: Business breakdown: Web3Forms — Contact Form API for Modern Websites

pick.topic: Business breakdown: Web3Forms — Contact Form API for Modern Websites
pick.angle: A boring contact-form API makes about $44K/month, and the site is a single simple product anyone can look at

research.what_it_does: A contact form API: you point a plain HTML form at their endpoint with an access key, and submissions land in your email inbox. You need no server or backend code.
research.who_pays: Mostly web developers, freelancers and agencies who build static or Jamstack sites. They upgrade for higher volume, file uploads, autoresponders and a longer submission history.
research.pricing: Free plan: 250 submissions/month, unlimited forms and domains. Pro: $15/month or $149/year for 10,000 submissions/month. Agency: $39/month or $399/year for 20,000 submissions/month. A yearly-only $49/year plan with 5,000 submissions/month is by application, for students, startups and non-profits. These figures come from third-party readings of web3forms.com/pricing dated Oct 2026, not the page itself. The page shows prices in the visitor's local currency, so the writer should check it before filming.
growth: Launch: the founder launched on Twitter and shared it in a few Reddit and Telegram groups, which gave him beta testers (Indie Hustle interview). He said it then grew 'really slowly' and that he didn't actively promote it apart from sharing stats on Twitter.

SEO: the founder says he put effort into SEO from the early days. He created content so Google could pick up many related keywords, and says Google is currently the #1 acquisition channel (Indie Hustle interview).

SEO, long-term content: Starter Story says he planned a long-term game of adding articles and free resources such as contact form templates to attract people searching for a contact form for static websites.

Build in public: his Indie Hackers log has monthly transparency reports. The Feb 2021 report listed 2.76k page views, 1.5k unique visitors, 205 free users, 11 paid users (+2) and $101.60 revenue (+12.7%).
Paid promo test: on Jan 20, 2021 he promoted it on the Instagram page 'Meet the Dev'. The page owner had approached him, and he tried it as a test (Indie Hackers log).

Slow early revenue: Gaps (citing the founder) says that by mid-2023 he had reached $5,000 in annual recurring revenue. By Nov 2024 it had 100+ paying customers and $1,600 MRR. That figure conflicts with the Stripe/Paddle-verified $44k MRR now, so treat the Gaps number as stale or incomplete.

Distribution via the pricing model: there is a free tier with 250 submissions/month. AlternativeTo and review sites describe it as the largest metered monthly free tier in the category. Those are third-party comparisons, not founder statements.
founder_story: Surjith S M is a front-end developer and designer from Kerala, India, and an indie maker since about 2015. He started out freelancing and selling website templates on Envato Market (AI4Chat, Indie Maker List).

He says he built it out of his own need. Jamstack static sites could be hosted free, but there was no good way to add a contact form, and he found nothing that fit, so he built his own (Indie Hustle).

He built a proof of concept and tested it over the Christmas holidays, then opened the beta in December 2020 (AI4Chat, Indie Hackers). Indie Maker List lists it as one of his active products, alongside Web3Templates, Astroship and Stablo.
He is the sole listed founder, and TrustMRR lists no funding (bootstrapped).
lessons: Build the tool you can't find. He was a template seller who needed a form backend for static sites, found nothing that fit, and built it. His own use case was the first market.
Start SEO and content on day one, even if it's slow. He says early SEO effort now makes Google his #1 channel. The curve was slow: about $100/mo early on, $5K ARR by mid-2023, and $44K MRR in 2026.

A generous free tier can work as the funnel. 250 free submissions a month and unlimited forms drive adoption among developers, and the paid plans sell volume, uploads and history. TrustMRR counts about 412,000 users against 3,204 active subscriptions.
criticism: Crowded market: Formspree, Formbold, Static Forms, Getform/Forminit, Netlify Forms and splitforms all compete, and several publish pages aimed at Web3Forms users. Competitors also say it gives less volume per dollar than they do, and note that file uploads and autoresponders need the Pro plan.
Revenue is not profit. TrustMRR hides the margin, though one cached snapshot of its page showed a '95% profit margin'. That is unverified here.
Growth is now flat, about 1% month-over-month on TrustMRR.
Free users heavily outnumber paying ones (about 412,000 users vs 3,204 subscriptions), and the free tier limits history to 30 days.
Early traction was very slow. The business took years to reach meaningful revenue.
facts: TrustMRR (Stripe-verified, via Paddle API key): $44,110 MRR, $45,577 revenue in the last 30 days, $359,894 all-time, 3,204 active subscriptions, rank #268, about 412,000 users, founded December 2020, bootstrapped.
Indie Hackers log: Feb 2021 revenue was $101.60 with 11 paid users and 205 free users.
Starter Story headline: 'How Web3Forms Reached 3,000 Users With a Simple Contact Form Solution'. Its revenue figures ($417K/month, $5M/year, started 2019) are clearly wrong, so don't use them.
The Indie Hustle interview is titled 'A no-code side project making $10,000' and covers annual revenue at the time. It is undated in the results, so verify before quoting.
TrustMRR lists the stack as Next.js, Tailwind, Vercel, Hetzner, Cloudflare and Paddle. Starter Story says it was built as a serverless API on AWS.
The 7-day refund policy comes from a third-party summary (form2lead). Verify on the page.
do_not_claim: Profit or profit margin (hidden on TrustMRR, and the 95% figure is unverified)
Team size beyond 'founder-led' (only one founder is listed, and no source confirms no employees)
That the founder has a large X following as a launch driver (TrustMRR lists 10.2k followers, but no source credits X for the growth)
Any Starter Story revenue numbers ($417K/month, $5M/year, 2019 start)
Exact current prices unless the pricing page is checked (they show in local currency, and third parties list different figures such as $12, $13 or $18/mo)
A specific viral moment or Product Hunt launch (none found)
That the Instagram promo produced customers (the result wasn't found)
Total time to reach $44K MRR as a single clean timeline (the Gaps $1.6K MRR from Nov 2024 conflicts with the current verified numbers)
research.notes: I couldn't open the official pricing page. The pricing and the 'show' strings come from third-party summaries, so confirm the exact on-page text ('$149', '250 submissions', 'It's free!') before recording. Prices display in local currency by visitor location. TrustMRR's 'Founder' line shows his X handle as @surjithctly. The 'Web3' in the name is not about crypto: the product is a plain HTML form backend, so don't pitch it as a crypto or blockchain tool. The Indie Hustle and Indie Hackers sources are older, from 2021 to about 2024, so frame the growth as a slow build over about 6 years. Starter Story says 'Reached 3,000 Users' while TrustMRR shows 3,204 subscriptions, so don't mix users and subscribers.

Value proposition: Receive your html contact form submissions directly in your email inbox using our contact form api service. No server or backend code needed. It's free!
Problem solved: Setting up form is a pain. Web3Forms works without any server or backend code like PHP, allowing users to receive contact form data without using backend code or databases.

Tech stack backend: Vercel, Hetzner, Cloudflare, Paddle
